title: Activepieces alternatives, with checked prices | 50agents
description: Activepieces alternatives: n8n to keep self-hosting with more integrations, Make or Zapier for hosted apps, and 50agents to build from plain words.
answer: If you chose Activepieces to self-host and now need more integrations, n8n is the other mature self-hosted option, with 2,829 integrations listed against Activepieces' 770+.
If you no longer want to run it yourself, Make and Zapier are the hosted choices with the most apps, and 50agents builds the automation from plain words.
ask: Set up an AI agent that sends me tomorrow's meetings from Google Calendar in Slack every day at 18:00
lede: The usual reason to move is a missing app: Activepieces lists 770+, fewer than Zapier, Make or n8n.

entries.suits: Teams where one person runs Activepieces and everyone else sends them requests. The person who needs a workflow asks Captain for it and approves the plan.
entries.limit: No self-hosting and no open-source core. If running on your own servers is why you chose Activepieces, 50agents is not a replacement.

entries.suits: Developers who want to keep self-hosting and need more integrations, a Code node in JavaScript or Python, and human approval for AI tool calls.
entries.price: No free cloud plan. Starter: €20 a month billed yearly (2.5K executions)
entries.limit: There is no free cloud plan, and cloud prices are in euros and billed yearly.

entries.suits: Teams ready to stop hosting who want a visual builder with more apps and JSON blueprints they can export.
entries.price: Free: 1,000 credits a month. Core: from $9 a month (10,000 credits)
entries.limit: Billed per credit, with most actions costing one, so long flows cost more per run than on a flat plan.

entries.suits: Teams whose main problem was missing apps: Zapier lists 10,541+.
entries.price: Free: 100 tasks a month. Professional: $19.99 a month billed yearly (750 tasks)
entries.limit: Every action step is a task, and the free plan is two-step Zaps only.

entries.suits: Teams inside Microsoft 365 who can use the free licence for cloud flows with standard connectors.
entries.price: Free for cloud flows with standard connectors. Premium: $15.00 per user a month, paid yearly
entries.limit: The free licence cannot share flows and covers standard connectors only.

us: The people who need automations will never open a flow builder.
You would rather not run or update a server.
Some jobs need an AI agent's judgement or an app with its own records.
them: You need air-gapped or on-premises installs. Activepieces documents both; of the others here, only n8n self-hosts.
You want a flat team price: Plus is $20 a month for up to 5 users, not per seat.
Your apps are all in its 770+, or you are happy to write the missing pieces.

move.title: List flows and the pieces they use
move.body: Note each flow's trigger, its pieces and any inline code. Code steps are the hardest to move, so flag them.

move.title: Check every app in the new catalog
move.body: Look each piece up in the new tool's app directory before you commit; this is where moves usually stall.

move.title: Move the AI-heavy flows first
move.body: AI steps cost the most credits on Activepieces, so they show the savings, or the lack of them, fastest.

move.title: Keep the old instance running for a month
move.body: Turn flows off one by one rather than shutting the server down.

faqs.a: Its Free plan gives 1,000 credits, unlimited flows and up to 5 users, with no card. Self-hosting the MIT-licensed core is also an option.

faqs.q: What is the best open-source alternative to Activepieces?
faqs.a: n8n is the most established self-hosted alternative. Its pricing page says a self-hosted version is available on GitHub; read the licence in its repository before you rely on it.
Not for workflows. Pipedream's docs say its workflows are shutting down, and it now sells Connect, an integration layer for developers.
